correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the amplitude independently with the orthonormal sine eigenvectors sin(πkj/6)/√3 for k,j=1,…,5. Expanding its squared modulus directly by the ten unordered spectral pairs gives a constant term and six columns indexed by distinct positive gaps. Exact algebra in Q(√3) gives column rank six across the 15 upper-triangular entries, and all residuals at the stated six cosine moments are zero. This proves necessity and sufficiency for every law, without a symmetry hypothesis. On the auxiliary torus, the two stated densities have positive lower bounds, unit integrals and the required Fourier coefficients; independence and evenness give the zero cross terms. Positive full support puts the barycenter in the relative interior: a supporting affine functional nonconstant on the image cannot have zero integral of its nonnegative slack. For any fixed second angle φ, times φ+2πn with n arbitrarily large give that angle exactly and give dense first angles by irrational rotation. Thus every tail has the same compact convex closure, and its convex hull contains the relative interior (approximate the vertices of a simplex enclosing the target strictly). Carathéodory in dimension six, removal of zero weights and merging equal times establish the stated finite real-time law.

originality.rationale: Kang, arXiv:2609.14463v1 (13 September 2026 UTC), already proves finite uniform readout for the same adjacency path at q=N+1 equal to twice a prime, hence q=6. Kang's forced-coherence lemma and its converse specialize exactly to the six numbers in the Finding. His proof uses torus-density, relative interior and Carathéodory. Restricting to any tail preserves its closure by irrational rotation, and counting the six distinct cosine gaps in the same expansion reduces the generic bound 10 to 7. The sharper printed bound and tail quantifier are not quoted as printed in Kang; they are routine specializations of the prior proof, not an independent solution of the P5 existence question.

value.rationale: Exact mixing on an ordinary path from all initial vertices is a meaningful problem, but the prior general theorem already settles this instance. The surviving display is a table of repeated gaps evaluated at a five-point spectrum and a routine dimension tightening of a general Carathéodory bound. It neither gives an optimal support result nor a new construction of exact observation times, and tail density already holds in the prior proof. There is no independently valuable new result here to salvage by changing the introduction or adding verification.
residual_risks: This does not evaluate the value of an explicitly constructed law, a sharp minimal support theorem, or any other previously unresolved graph instance.
